title: Lior and the Asset
premise: Marguerite Okafor, a financial-crimes investigator who launders reputations for the powerful, receives calls on a burner phone from a voice they buried years ago: their presumed-dead mentor, Elias Vance, who faked his death to escape the syndicate they both served. The syndicate's ledger—the 'Asset'—has surfaced, and both the criminals and a federal task force will kill to control it. Marguerite must choose between protecting the found family of misfits who owe them everything and exposing the truth that could destroy them all. In the end, Marguerite trades their own anonymity—surrendering themselves to federal custody in exchange for immunity for their people—and discovers that belonging was never something they had to buy.
about_author: Jude Delacroix is the pen name of a former compliance officer who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people who live in the gaps between ledgers.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A routine job scrubbing a senator's offshore trail establishes their world of invisible work and paid silence. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the ache of being useful and unseen.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A burner phone arrives with no sender; it rings once at midnight. The voice on the line is Elias Vance—dead for six years. Beat: vertigo, grief cracked open.

chapters.title: Six Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Marguerite's POV. How Elias recruited them, built their crew of castoffs, and apparently died in a warehouse fire. Beat: tenderness and old guilt.

chapters.title: The Crew
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV introduces the found family: hacker Priya, ex-cop Dov, forger Camille. They notice Marguerite is rattled but say nothing. Beat: warmth under surveillance.

chapters.title: Proof of Life
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alive in hiding, he explains the Asset—a master ledger implicating everyone he ever protected—and why only Marguerite can move it. Beat: desperate trust.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. He spots surveillance on the crew's safehouse and tells no one, running his own quiet investigation. Beat: protective dread.

chapters.title: The Task Force
chapters.summary: Special Agent Renata Cole's POV. She's spent three years chasing the syndicate and has just identified Marguerite as its launderer. Beat: cold ambition sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Cole approaches Marguerite in a parking garage with an offer: flip on the syndicate or be buried with it. Beat: cornered calculation.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Elias reveals names on the Asset—including Marguerite's own and Camille's. Beat: betrayal braided with loyalty.

chapters.title: Camille's Hands
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. She recognizes the forged documents circulating in the case and realizes her past work is the thread that could hang them all. Beat: fear of one's own craftsmanship.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Rules
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Elias meet in person at a shuttered aquarium. He lays out rules: trust no one fully, move the ledger in pieces. Beat: reunion shadowed by doubt—is he really Elias?

chapters.title: Doubt
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She runs biometric analysis on a photo Elias sent and finds anomalies. She tells Marguerite nothing yet. Beat: loyalty versus suspicion.

chapters.title: A Favor Called In
chapters.summary: Marguerite leans on an old client, banker Odile Ferrand, to trace the burner phone's origin. Beat: transactional intimacy, debts as currency.

chapters.title: The Syndicate Wakes
chapters.summary: Syndicate lieutenant Marek Voss's POV. The fire six years ago didn't finish the job; orders come down to find the ledger and the traitor. Beat: patient menace.

chapters.title: Tail
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. He shakes a tail and confirms two separate watchers: feds and syndicate. The crew is boxed in. Beat: the protector realizing protection may be impossible.

chapters.title: Family Dinner
chapters.summary: Marguerite hosts a deliberately ordinary dinner, watching each crew member, wondering who might break first. Beat: love as reconnaissance.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She agrees to help—for a cut of whatever the ledger is worth, and a favor to be named later. Beat: greed wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Split the Asset
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Following Elias's plan, they fragment the ledger across three dead drops. Beat: purpose returning, adrenaline over dread.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Voss's men hit what they think is a drop; instead they grab a courier who knows nothing. Marguerite learns of it too late. Beat: guilt as accelerant.

chapters.title: Cole Closes In
chapters.summary: Cole's POV. She flips the captured courier and gets a partial description of Marguerite's operation. Beat: the net tightening with procedural calm.

chapters.title: Priya Tells
chapters.summary: Priya finally shows Marguerite the biometric anomalies: the man calling himself Elias may be a surgically altered double. Beat: shattering of the last certainty.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Aquarium
chapters.summary: Marguerite confronts Elias. He admits the face is new but insists the mission—and the danger—are real. Beat: choosing faith without proof.

chapters.title: The Double Game
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They decide to play all sides: feed Cole enough to keep her close, feed Voss false drops, keep Elias's plan alive. Beat: exhilaration curdling into exhaustion.

chapters.title: Camille Breaks
chapters.summary: Camille, terrified, makes a private deal with Voss to protect her daughter. Beat: love weaponized against loyalty.

chapters.title: The False Drop
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. He runs a decoy drop that draws syndicate shooters into a federal ambush. Bodies fall; the war goes loud. Beat: grim triumph.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The crew regroups in a safehouse that no longer feels safe. Camille won't meet anyone's eyes. Beat: the family cracking along fault lines.

chapters.title: Odile Sells Them
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She sells the drop locations to Voss, cashing her favor early. Beat: banal betrayal over champagne.

chapters.title: Ambush
chapters.summary: Syndicate raid on the safehouse. Priya is shot covering the others' escape; Dov carries her out. Beat: terror, sacrifice, the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Hospital Hours
chapters.summary: Marguerite keeps vigil while Priya fights for her life. Cole appears—not to arrest, but to warn: Voss has ordered Marguerite's death tonight. Beat: enemies finding common ground.

chapters.title: The Real Ledger
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He confesses the truth: there is no physical ledger. The Asset is a person—his daughter, raised inside the syndicate, carrying everything in her memory. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV (introduced). Nineteen, guarded, she has memorized the syndicate's entire architecture and trusts no one—least of all her father. Beat: ferocious isolation meeting offered shelter.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Dov extract Nadia from a syndicate schoolhouse as Voss's men close in. Beat: white-knuckle action, first spark of belonging.

chapters.title: Voss's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Voss contacts Marguerite directly: deliver Nadia by dawn or the crew dies one by one, starting with Camille. Beat: ultimatum as mirror—what would you trade?

chapters.title: Camille's Confession
chapters.summary: Camille admits her deal to the crew, expecting exile. Instead Marguerite forgives her—conditionally. Beat: forgiveness as the family's true currency.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the exchange site, Marguerite offers Voss not Nadia but themselves: testimony dismantling the syndicate's finances, if the crew walks free. Beat: self-sacrifice as the secret worth killing for.

chapters.title: Double-Cross
chapters.summary: Voss takes the offer and orders deaths anyway. Elias intervenes, taking bullets meant for Marguerite—this time dying for real. Beat: climax, grief and fury fused.

chapters.title: Burn It Down
chapters.summary: Marguerite, Cole, and the wounded crew combine forces: Priya's data, Camille's forgeries reversed, Dov's tactics. Voss is taken alive. Beat: catharsis through competence and solidarity.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Marguerite negotiates with Cole: full confession and cooperation in exchange for immunity for the crew and protection for Nadia. Beat: surrender as the bravest act.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Crew POVs interwoven. Goodbyes at the courthouse steps; Nadia chooses to stay with Priya and Dov rather than vanish again. Beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: The Visitor
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Marguerite's POV. Months into cooperation, in a secure facility, a new burner phone rings. A familiar voice says Marguerite's name. Beat: hope and dread entwined—family, it seems, always calls collect.
